place.en: outside the outer gate of Anling

manner.en: beheaded in court robes at the Eastern Market
died of illness on the road

units.zh: 袁盎者，楚人也，字絲。
units.en: Yuan Ang was a native of Chu, and his courtesy name was Si.
units.literal: Yuan Ang was a man of Chu, with the courtesy name Si.

units.zh: 父故為群盜，徙處安陵。
units.en: His father had once been a bandit and was later resettled in Anling.
units.literal: His father had formerly been among a band of robbers, and was relocated to settle in Anling.

units.zh: 高后時，盎嘗為呂祿舍人。
units.en: During the reign of Empress Dowager Gao, Ang served as a retainer in the household of Lü Lu.
units.literal: During the time of Empress Dowager Gao, Ang once served as a retainer of Lü Lu.

units.zh: 及孝文帝即位，盎兄噲任盎為中郎。
units.en: When Emperor Wen came to the throne, Ang's elder brother Kuai secured him a position as Gentleman of the Palace.
units.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen ascended the throne, Ang's elder brother Kuai recommended Ang to serve as a Gentleman of the Palace.

units.zh: 絳侯為丞相，朝罷趨出，意得甚。
units.en: The Marquis of Jiang served as Chancellor, and whenever court was dismissed, he would stride out looking enormously pleased with himself.
units.literal: When the Marquis of Jiang served as Chancellor, after court sessions he would hasten out with a look of great self-satisfaction.

units.zh: 上禮之恭，常自送之。
units.en: The Emperor showed him such deference that he would personally see him off.
units.literal: The Emperor treated him with such reverent courtesy that he would personally escort him out.

units.zh: 袁盎進曰：「陛下以丞相何如人？」
units.en: Yuan Ang came forward and asked, 'Your Majesty, what sort of man do you think the Chancellor is?'
units.literal: Yuan Ang stepped forward and said: 'Your Majesty, what kind of man do you consider the Chancellor to be?'

units.zh: 上曰：「社稷臣。」
units.en: The Emperor replied, 'A pillar of the state.'
units.literal: The Emperor said: 'A minister of the altars of state.'

units.zh: 盎曰：「絳侯所謂功臣，非社稷臣，社稷臣主在與在，主亡與亡。
units.en: Ang said, 'The Marquis of Jiang is a meritorious minister, not a pillar of the state. A true pillar of the state shares his sovereign's fate—he rises with his lord and falls with him.
units.literal: Ang said: 'The Marquis of Jiang is what is called a meritorious minister, not a minister of the altars of state. A minister of the altars of state lives when the sovereign lives and perishes when the sovereign perishes.

units.zh: 方呂后時，諸呂用事，擅相王，劉氏不絕如帶。
units.en: When Empress Lü ruled, her kinsmen seized power, appointing chancellors and kings at will, and the House of Liu survived by only a thread.
units.literal: During the time of Empress Lü, the Lü clan held power, freely appointing chancellors and kings, and the survival of the Liu clan hung by a thread like a thin ribbon.

units.zh: 是時絳侯為太尉，主兵柄，弗能正。
units.en: At that time, the Marquis of Jiang was Grand Commandant with command of the armies, yet he could not set things right.
units.literal: At that time the Marquis of Jiang held the post of Grand Commandant, commanding military authority, yet he could not set things right.

units.zh: 呂后崩，大臣相與共畔諸呂，太尉主兵，適會其成功，所謂功臣，非社稷臣。
units.en: After Empress Lü died, the senior ministers banded together to overthrow the Lü clan. The Grand Commandant led the troops and happened to be there when success was achieved. That makes him a meritorious minister, not a pillar of the state.
units.literal: When Empress Lü died, the great ministers joined together to overthrow the Lü clan. The Grand Commandant commanded the troops and happened to be present for the achievement of success. This is what is called a meritorious minister, not a minister of the altars of state.

units.zh: 丞相如有驕主色。
units.en: The Chancellor carries himself with an air of arrogance toward Your Majesty.
units.literal: The Chancellor seems to show an air of arrogance toward the sovereign.

units.zh: 陛下謙讓，臣主失禮，竊為陛下不取也。」
units.en: Your Majesty has been humble and yielding, but the proper decorum between sovereign and minister has been lost. I venture to say that this is beneath Your Majesty.'
units.literal: Your Majesty shows humility and deference, yet the proper rites between minister and sovereign are lost. I privately consider this inadvisable for Your Majesty.'

units.zh: 後朝，上益莊，丞相益畏。
units.en: From then on, the Emperor grew more commanding at court, and the Chancellor became ever more apprehensive.
units.literal: At subsequent court sessions, the Emperor became increasingly dignified, and the Chancellor became increasingly fearful.

units.zh: 已而絳侯望袁盎曰：「吾與而兄善，今兒廷毀我！」
units.en: Before long, the Marquis of Jiang confronted Yuan Ang with a glare and said, 'I was on good terms with your brother, and now you, boy, denounce me at court!'
units.literal: Soon after, the Marquis of Jiang glared at Yuan Ang resentfully and said: 'I was on good terms with your brother, and now you, boy, slander me at court!'

units.zh: 盎遂不謝。
units.en: Ang offered no apology.
units.literal: Ang thereupon did not apologize.

units.zh: 及絳侯免相之國，國人上書告以為反，徵系清室，宗室諸公莫敢為言，唯袁盎明絳侯無罪。
units.en: When the Marquis of Jiang was dismissed from the chancellorship and returned to his fief, someone from his domain submitted a memorial accusing him of rebellion. He was summoned and confined in the imperial prison. Not a single member of the imperial clan or the senior ministers dared to speak in his defense—only Yuan Ang declared the Marquis of Jiang to be innocent.
units.literal: When the Marquis of Jiang was dismissed as Chancellor and returned to his fief, someone from his domain submitted a memorial accusing him of plotting rebellion. He was summoned and imprisoned in the special detention cells. None of the members of the imperial clan or senior officials dared speak on his behalf. Only Yuan Ang testified that the Marquis of Jiang was innocent.

units.zh: 絳侯得釋，盎頗有力。
units.en: When the Marquis of Jiang was released, it was largely thanks to Ang's efforts.
units.literal: When the Marquis of Jiang was released, Ang had contributed considerably to the effort.

units.zh: 絳侯乃大與盎結交。
units.en: From then on, the Marquis of Jiang became a close friend and ally of Ang.
units.literal: The Marquis of Jiang thereupon formed a deep friendship with Ang.

units.zh: 淮南厲王朝，殺辟陽侯，居處驕甚。
units.en: The Fierce King of Huainan came to court, killed the Marquis of Biyang, and behaved with extreme arrogance.
units.literal: The Fierce King of Huainan came to court, killed the Marquis of Biyang, and conducted himself with extreme arrogance.

units.zh: 袁盎諫曰：「諸侯大驕必生患，可適削地。」
units.en: Yuan Ang remonstrated, 'When feudal lords grow too proud, disaster is sure to follow. You should discipline him by reducing his territory.'
units.literal: Yuan Ang remonstrated, saying: 'When feudal lords become too arrogant, trouble is sure to follow. It would be best to punish him by reducing his territory.'

units.zh: 上弗用。
units.en: The Emperor did not heed his advice.
units.literal: The Emperor did not adopt his advice.

units.zh: 淮南王益橫。
units.en: The King of Huainan became increasingly lawless.
units.literal: The King of Huainan grew ever more unruly.

units.zh: 及棘蒲侯柴武太子謀反事覺，治，連淮南王，淮南王徵，上因遷之蜀，轞車傳送。
units.en: When the plot of the heir of the Marquis of Jipu Chai Wu was uncovered and investigated, the trail led to the King of Huainan. The king was summoned, and the Emperor ordered him banished to Shu, to be transported in a prisoner's cart from station to station.
units.literal: When the conspiracy of the heir of the Marquis of Jipu, Chai Wu, was discovered and investigated, the case implicated the King of Huainan. The King of Huainan was summoned, and the Emperor ordered him exiled to Shu, transported by prisoner's cart through relay stations.

units.zh: 袁盎時為中郎將，乃諫曰：「陛下素驕淮南王，弗稍禁，以至此，今又暴摧折之。
units.en: Yuan Ang, then serving as Commander of the Gentlemen of the Palace, remonstrated, 'Your Majesty has always indulged the King of Huainan and never reined him in, which is how things came to this pass. Now you would break him all at once.
units.literal: Yuan Ang, who was then serving as Commander of the Gentlemen of the Palace, remonstrated: 'Your Majesty has long indulged the King of Huainan and never gradually restrained him, which has brought matters to this point. Now you would suddenly crush him.

units.zh: 淮南王為人剛，如有遇霧露行道死，陛下竟為以天下之大弗能容，有殺弟之名，柰何？」
units.en: The King of Huainan is a man of unyielding spirit. If he should fall ill on the road and die from exposure, Your Majesty will be seen as one who, despite ruling all under heaven, could not abide his own brother—and will bear the name of a fratricide. What then?'
units.literal: The King of Huainan is a man of unyielding temperament. If he should encounter fog and dew on the road and die of illness, Your Majesty would ultimately bear the reputation that, possessing all the vastness of the realm, you could not make room for your own brother, gaining the name of one who killed his brother. What then?'

units.zh: 上弗聽，遂行之。
units.en: The Emperor refused to listen and carried out the order.
units.literal: The Emperor did not listen and proceeded with the order.

units.zh: 淮南王至雍，病死，聞，上輟食，哭甚哀。
units.en: The King of Huainan died of illness on the road at Yong. When the Emperor received the news, he stopped eating and wept bitterly.
units.literal: When the King of Huainan reached Yong, he fell ill and died. When the Emperor heard the news, he stopped eating and wept in deep sorrow.

units.zh: 盎入，頓首請罪。
units.en: Ang came before the Emperor, kowtowed, and begged to be punished.
units.literal: Ang entered and, bowing his head to the ground, begged forgiveness for his offense.

units.zh: 上曰：「以不用公言至此。」
units.en: The Emperor said, 'It is because I did not listen to you that things have come to this.'
units.literal: The Emperor said: 'It is because I did not heed your words that things have come to this.'

units.zh: 盎曰：「上自寬，此往事，豈可悔哉！
units.en: Ang said, 'Your Majesty should put this behind you. The matter is past—regret will not undo it.
units.literal: Ang said: 'May Your Majesty take comfort. This is a matter of the past—how can it be undone through regret?

units.zh: 且陛下有高世之行者三，此不足以毀名。」
units.en: Moreover, Your Majesty has three deeds that surpass those of any age, and this alone is not enough to tarnish your name.'
units.literal: Moreover, Your Majesty has three deeds that surpass all others of this age, and this alone is not enough to tarnish your reputation.'

units.zh: 上曰：「吾高世行三者何事？」
units.en: The Emperor asked, 'What are these three surpassing deeds of mine?'
units.literal: The Emperor said: 'What are these three deeds of mine that surpass the age?'

units.zh: 盎曰：「陛下居代時，太后嘗病，三年，陛下不交睫，不解衣，湯藥非陛下口所嘗弗進。
units.en: Ang said, 'When Your Majesty was King of Dai, the Empress Dowager fell ill, and for three years you never closed your eyes to rest, never changed your robes, and refused to let any medicine be given to her unless you had tasted it first.
units.literal: Ang said: 'When Your Majesty resided in Dai, the Empress Dowager once fell ill for three years. During that time, Your Majesty never closed your eyes to sleep, never removed your robes, and would not allow any medicine to be administered unless you had first tasted it yourself.

units.zh: 夫曾參以布衣猶難之，今陛下親以王者修之，過曾參孝遠矣。
units.en: Even Zeng Shen, a commoner, found such devotion difficult to sustain. Yet Your Majesty practiced it as a king, far surpassing the filial piety of Zeng Shen.
units.literal: Even Zeng Shen, as a commoner, found such devotion difficult. Now Your Majesty has personally practiced it as a king, surpassing the filial piety of Zeng Shen by far.

units.zh: 夫諸呂用事，大臣專制，然陛下從代乘六傳馳不測之淵，雖賁育之勇不及陛下。
units.en: When the Lü clan held power and the ministers ruled as they pleased, Your Majesty rode from Dai by relay carriage and plunged headlong into an abyss of danger. Even the legendary warriors Ben and Yu could not match such courage.
units.literal: When the Lü clan held power and the great ministers ruled arbitrarily, Your Majesty rode from Dai by relay carriages and raced into an unfathomable abyss of danger. Even the courage of Ben and Yu could not match Your Majesty's.

units.zh: 陛下至代邸，西向讓天子位者再，南面讓天子位者三。
units.en: When Your Majesty arrived at the Dai residence, you declined the throne twice while facing west, and three more times while facing south.
units.literal: When Your Majesty arrived at the residence of the King of Dai, you twice declined the throne while facing west, and three times declined it while facing south.

units.zh: 夫許由一讓，而陛下五以天下讓，過許由四矣。
units.en: The sage Xu You declined the throne once, but Your Majesty declined the empire five times, surpassing Xu You fourfold.
units.literal: Xu You declined once, yet Your Majesty declined the empire five times—surpassing Xu You by four.

units.zh: 且陛下遷淮南王，欲以苦其志，使改過，有司衛不謹，故病死。」
units.en: Moreover, when Your Majesty exiled the King of Huainan, the intention was to chasten his spirit and bring him to repentance. It was the negligence of the escorting officials that caused his death.'
units.literal: Moreover, when Your Majesty exiled the King of Huainan, the intention was to discipline his spirit and cause him to mend his ways. It was the negligence of the officials guarding him that led to his death from illness.'

units.zh: 於是上乃解，曰：「將柰何？」
units.en: At this the Emperor's spirits lifted, and he asked, 'What should be done?'
units.literal: At this the Emperor's grief was eased, and he said: 'What should be done now?'

units.zh: 盎曰：「淮南王有三子，唯在陛下耳。」
units.en: Ang said, 'The King of Huainan had three sons. The matter rests entirely with Your Majesty.'
units.literal: Ang said: 'The King of Huainan has three sons. It is entirely up to Your Majesty.'

units.zh: 於是文帝立其三子皆為王。
units.en: Emperor Wen then enfeoffed all three of the late king's sons as kings.
units.literal: Thereupon Emperor Wen enfeoffed all three of the King's sons as kings.

units.zh: 盎由此名重朝廷。
units.en: From then on, Ang's reputation carried great weight at court.
units.literal: From this, Ang's reputation gained great weight at court.

units.zh: 袁盎常引大體慨。
units.en: Yuan Ang always spoke of matters of great principle with impassioned conviction.
units.literal: Yuan Ang always drew upon matters of great principle and spoke with impassioned concern.

units.zh: 宦者趙同以數幸，常害袁盎，袁盎患之。
units.en: The eunuch Zhao Tong, who had long enjoyed the Emperor's favor, constantly sought to undermine Yuan Ang, and Ang was troubled by this.
units.literal: The eunuch Zhao Tong, who enjoyed frequent imperial favor, constantly sought to harm Yuan Ang, and Yuan Ang was troubled by this.

units.zh: 盎兄子種為常侍騎，持節夾乘，說盎曰：「君與鬬，廷辱之，使其毀不用。」
units.en: Ang's nephew Zhong served as an Attendant Cavalry officer who rode beside the imperial carriage bearing a tally. He advised Ang, 'Pick a fight with him and humiliate him at court, so that his slanders lose their sting.'
units.literal: Ang's nephew Zhong served as an Attendant Cavalry officer and rode alongside the imperial carriage bearing a tally. He advised Ang: 'You should clash with him and humiliate him at court, so that his slanders lose their effect.'

units.zh: 孝文帝出，趙同參乘，袁盎伏車前曰：「臣聞天子所與共六尺輿者，皆天下豪英。
units.en: When Emperor Wen went out, Zhao Tong rode as a companion in the imperial carriage. Yuan Ang threw himself before the carriage and said, 'I have heard that those who share the Son of Heaven's carriage should be the finest heroes of the realm.
units.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen went out, Zhao Tong rode as a companion in the imperial carriage. Yuan Ang prostrated himself before the carriage and said: 'I have heard that those who share the six-foot carriage with the Son of Heaven should all be the outstanding heroes of the realm.

units.zh: 今漢雖乏人，陛下獨奈何與刀鋸餘人載！」
units.en: Though the Han may be short of men, how can Your Majesty ride with the leavings of the knife and saw!'
units.literal: Although the Han dynasty may lack men, how can Your Majesty alone ride with a remnant of the knife and saw!'

units.zh: 於是上笑，下趙同。
units.en: The Emperor laughed and ordered Zhao Tong to get off.
units.literal: At this the Emperor laughed and ordered Zhao Tong to step down.

units.zh: 趙同泣下車。
units.en: Zhao Tong climbed down from the carriage in tears.
units.literal: Zhao Tong wept as he descended from the carriage.

units.zh: 文帝從霸陵上，欲西馳下峻阪。
units.en: Emperor Wen ascended the heights at Baling and wanted to gallop down the steep western slope.
units.literal: Emperor Wen ascended the heights at Baling and wished to gallop westward down the steep slope.

units.zh: 袁盎騎，并車擥轡。
units.en: Yuan Ang rode up beside the carriage and seized the reins.
units.literal: Yuan Ang rode up alongside the carriage and seized the reins.

units.zh: 上曰：「將軍怯邪？」
units.en: The Emperor said, 'Are you afraid, General?'
units.literal: The Emperor said: 'Is the General a coward?'

units.zh: 盎曰：「臣聞千金之子坐不垂堂，百金之子不騎衡，聖主不乘危而徼幸。
units.en: Ang replied, 'I have heard that a man whose family is worth a thousand in gold does not sit at the edge of the roof, a man worth a hundred in gold does not lean over a railing on horseback, and a wise sovereign does not court danger for the sake of a thrill.
units.literal: Ang said: 'I have heard that the son of a house worth a thousand gold pieces does not sit at the edge of the eaves, the son of a house worth a hundred gold pieces does not lean over a railing on horseback, and a sage ruler does not court danger for the sake of a thrill.

units.zh: 今陛下騁六騑，馳下峻山，如有馬驚車敗，陛下縱自輕，柰高廟、太后何？」
units.en: Now Your Majesty drives a team of six at full gallop down a steep mountain. If the horses bolt and the carriage overturns, even if Your Majesty makes light of your own life, what of the ancestral temple and the Empress Dowager?'
units.literal: Now Your Majesty drives six steeds at full gallop down a steep mountain. If a horse should bolt and the carriage overturn, even if Your Majesty makes light of your own person, what of the ancestral temple and the Empress Dowager?'

units.zh: 上乃止。
units.en: The Emperor relented.
units.literal: The Emperor thereupon stopped.

units.zh: 上幸上林，皇后、慎夫人從。
units.en: The Emperor went to the Shanglin Park with the Empress and Lady Shen in attendance.
units.literal: The Emperor visited the Shanglin Park, accompanied by the Empress and Lady Shen.

units.zh: 其在禁中，常同席坐。
units.en: In the palace, the two customarily sat side by side on the same mat.
units.literal: When they were in the palace, they customarily sat together on the same mat.

units.zh: 及坐，郎署長布席，袁盎引卻慎夫人坐。
units.en: When the seats were being arranged, the head of the Gentleman's Office laid out the mats, and Yuan Ang drew Lady Shen's seat back to a separate position.
units.literal: When they were about to sit, the head of the Gentleman's Office laid out the mats, and Yuan Ang pulled back Lady Shen's seat to a separate position.

units.zh: 慎夫人怒，不肯坐。
units.en: Lady Shen was furious and refused to sit down.
units.literal: Lady Shen was angry and refused to sit.

units.zh: 上亦怒，起，入禁中。
units.en: The Emperor was also angered. He stood and withdrew into the inner palace.
units.literal: The Emperor was also angered. He rose and withdrew into the inner palace.

units.zh: 盎因前說曰：「臣聞尊卑有序則上下和。
units.en: Ang then came forward and explained, 'I have heard that when the high and the low observe their proper order, harmony prevails between those above and those below.
units.literal: Ang thereupon came forward and explained: 'I have heard that when the noble and the base observe their proper order, harmony prevails between those above and below.

units.zh: 今陛下既已立后，慎夫人乃妾，妾主豈可與同坐哉！
units.en: Now that Your Majesty has installed the Empress, Lady Shen is a concubine. How can a concubine sit as an equal with her mistress!
units.literal: Now that Your Majesty has already established the Empress, Lady Shen is a concubine. How can a concubine and her mistress sit together as equals!

units.zh: 適所以失尊卑矣。
units.en: That is precisely how the distinction of rank is lost.
units.literal: This is precisely what undermines the distinction between the noble and the base.

units.zh: 且陛下幸之，即厚賜之。
units.en: If Your Majesty favors her, then shower her with gifts.
units.literal: Moreover, if Your Majesty favors her, then reward her generously.

units.zh: 陛下所以為慎夫人，適所以禍之。
units.en: What Your Majesty does for Lady Shen is precisely what will bring disaster upon her.
units.literal: What Your Majesty does for Lady Shen's sake is precisely what will bring disaster upon her.

units.zh: 陛下獨不見『人彘』乎？」
units.en: Has Your Majesty forgotten the fate of the Human Swine?'
units.literal: Has Your Majesty not seen what became of the "Human Swine"?'

units.zh: 於是上乃說，召語慎夫人。
units.en: At this the Emperor was persuaded. He summoned Lady Shen and explained Ang's reasoning to her.
units.literal: At this the Emperor was pleased. He summoned Lady Shen and told her what Ang had said.

units.zh: 慎夫人賜盎金五十斤。
units.en: Lady Shen presented Ang with fifty catties of gold.
units.literal: Lady Shen bestowed upon Ang fifty catties of gold.

units.zh: 然袁盎亦以數直諫，不得久居中，調為隴西都尉。
units.en: Yet because Yuan Ang had so often spoken bluntly in remonstrance, he could not remain long at court and was transferred to serve as Commandant of Longxi.
units.literal: However, because Yuan Ang had so often spoken bluntly in remonstrance, he could not remain long at the capital and was transferred to serve as Commandant of Longxi.

units.zh: 仁愛士卒，士卒皆爭為死。
units.en: He treated his soldiers with kindness and generosity, and they all competed for the chance to die for him.
units.literal: He treated the soldiers with benevolence and love, and the soldiers all vied to die for him.

units.zh: 遷為齊相。
units.en: He was then promoted to Chancellor of Qi.
units.literal: He was promoted to Chancellor of Qi.

units.zh: 徙為吳相，辭行，種謂盎曰：「吳王驕日久，國多姦。
units.en: He was transferred to serve as Chancellor of Wu. When he took his leave to depart, Zhong said to Ang, 'The King of Wu has been arrogant for years, and his kingdom is rife with sedition.
units.literal: He was transferred to serve as Chancellor of Wu. When he took his leave, Zhong said to Ang: 'The King of Wu has been arrogant for a long time, and his kingdom harbors many treacherous elements.

units.zh: 今茍欲劾治，彼不上書告君，即利劍刺君矣。
units.en: If you try to investigate and prosecute him, he will either submit a memorial denouncing you, or run you through with a sword.
units.literal: If you now try to impeach and bring order, he will either submit a memorial accusing you, or stab you with a sharp sword.

units.zh: 南方卑溼，君能日飲，毋何，時說王曰毋反而已。
units.en: The south is low and damp. Just drink every day, do nothing of consequence, and from time to time urge the king not to rebel. That is all you need to do.
units.literal: The south is low-lying and damp. You should just drink every day, do nothing, and from time to time persuade the king not to rebel—that is all.

units.zh: 如此幸得脫。」
units.en: If you do this, you may be lucky enough to escape with your life.'
units.literal: In this way you may be fortunate enough to escape with your life.'

units.zh: 盎用種之計，吳王厚遇盎。
units.en: Ang followed Zhong's advice, and the King of Wu treated him well.
units.literal: Ang followed Zhong's plan, and the King of Wu treated Ang generously.

units.zh: 盎告歸，道逢丞相申屠嘉，下車拜謁，丞相從車上謝袁盎。
units.en: When Ang took leave to return home, he met Chancellor Shentu Jia on the road. Ang descended from his carriage and bowed formally, but the Chancellor returned the greeting from his carriage without getting down.
units.literal: When Ang took leave to return home, he encountered Chancellor Shentu Jia on the road. Ang descended from his carriage and made a formal bow. The Chancellor merely returned the greeting from atop his carriage.

units.zh: 袁盎還，愧其吏，乃之丞相舍上謁，求見丞相。
units.en: When Yuan Ang returned, feeling humiliated in front of his attendants, he went to the Chancellor's residence, presented his card, and requested an audience.
units.literal: When Yuan Ang returned, feeling humiliated before his subordinates, he went to the Chancellor's residence, presented his calling card, and requested an audience.

units.zh: 丞相良久而見之。
units.en: The Chancellor kept him waiting a long while before receiving him.
units.literal: The Chancellor kept him waiting a long time before receiving him.

units.zh: 盎因跪曰：「願請閒。」
units.en: Ang knelt and said, 'I wish to speak with you in private.'
units.literal: Ang then knelt and said: 'I wish to request a private audience.'

units.zh: 丞相曰：「使君所言公事，之曹與長史掾議，吾且奏之；
units.en: The Chancellor said, 'If it is an official matter, discuss it with the Chief Clerk and his assistants in the bureau. I will then present it to the throne.
units.literal: The Chancellor said: 'If what you wish to say concerns official business, take it to the bureau and discuss it with the Chief Clerk and his assistants. I will then submit it to the throne.

units.zh: 即私邪，吾不受私語。」
units.en: If it is a private matter, I do not entertain private talk.'
units.literal: If it concerns private matters, I do not receive private speech.'

units.zh: 袁盎即跪說曰：「君為丞相，自度孰與陳平、絳侯？」
units.en: Yuan Ang knelt and asked, 'As Chancellor, how do you rate yourself against Chen Ping and the Marquis of Jiang?'
units.literal: Yuan Ang then knelt and said: 'As Chancellor, how do you compare yourself with Chen Ping and the Marquis of Jiang?'

units.zh: 丞相曰：「吾不如。」
units.en: The Chancellor replied, 'I am not their equal.'
units.literal: The Chancellor said: 'I am not their equal.'

units.zh: 袁盎曰：「善，君即自謂不如。
units.en: Yuan Ang said, 'Good—you yourself admit you are not their equal.
units.literal: Yuan Ang said: 'Good—you yourself admit you are not their equal.

units.zh: 夫陳平、絳侯輔翼高帝，定天下，為將相，而誅諸呂，存劉氏；
units.en: Chen Ping and the Marquis of Jiang upheld Emperor Gao, settled the empire, served as general and chancellor, and afterward wiped out the Lü clan, preserving the Liu house.
units.literal: Chen Ping and the Marquis of Jiang assisted Emperor Gao, pacified the realm, served as generals and chancellors, and later destroyed the Lü clan to preserve the House of Liu.

units.zh: 君乃為材官蹶張，遷為隊率，積功至淮陽守，非有奇計攻城野戰之功。
units.en: But you began as a crossbow soldier, rose to squad leader, and climbed through accumulated merit to Governor of Huaiyang—without a single brilliant stratagem or battlefield exploit to your name.
units.literal: But you began as a crossbow soldier, were promoted to squad leader, and accumulated merit until you became Governor of Huaiyang—without any brilliant stratagems, siege victories, or battlefield exploits.

units.zh: 且陛下從代來，每朝，郎官上書疏，未嘗不止輦受其言，言不可用置之，言可受採之，未嘗不稱善。
units.en: Moreover, since His Majesty came from Dai, whenever the Gentlemen submit memorials at court, he always stops his carriage to hear their words. Proposals he cannot use he sets aside; those he can accept he adopts, and he never fails to commend them.
units.literal: Moreover, since His Majesty came from Dai, at every court session, whenever the Gentlemen submit memorials, he invariably stops his carriage to receive their words. If a proposal is not useful, he sets it aside; if it is acceptable, he adopts it, and he never fails to praise it as good.

units.zh: 何也？
units.en: And why does he do this?
units.literal: Why is this?

units.zh: 則欲以致天下賢士大夫。
units.en: Because he wishes to draw the worthy men of the realm to his court.
units.literal: It is because he wishes to attract the worthy scholars and officials of the realm.

units.zh: 上日聞所不聞，明所不知，日益聖智；
units.en: Each day the Emperor learns what he did not know before, understands what was once obscure, and grows daily in wisdom.
units.literal: The Emperor daily hears what he had not heard before and understands what he had not known before, growing daily in sagely wisdom.

units.zh: 君今自閉鉗天下之口而日益愚。
units.en: Yet you shut yourself off and clamp shut the mouths of all under heaven, growing more foolish by the day.
units.literal: Yet you now shut yourself off and clamp shut the mouths of all under heaven, growing daily in foolishness.

units.zh: 夫以聖主責愚相，君受禍不久矣。」
units.en: When a wise sovereign calls a foolish chancellor to account, disaster will not be long in coming for you.'
units.literal: When a sagely sovereign holds a foolish chancellor to account, disaster will not be long in coming for you.'

units.zh: 丞相乃再拜曰：「嘉鄙野人，乃不知，將軍幸教。」
units.en: The Chancellor bowed twice and said, 'I, Jia, am but a crude and rustic man who did not understand. I am fortunate that the General has deigned to instruct me.'
units.literal: The Chancellor then bowed twice and said: 'Jia is but a crude and rustic man who did not understand. I am fortunate that the General has instructed me.'

units.zh: 引入與坐，為上客。
units.en: He invited Ang in to sit with him and treated him as a guest of honor.
units.literal: He invited Ang in to sit with him, treating him as an honored guest.

units.zh: 盎素不好鼂錯，鼂錯所居坐，盎去；
units.en: Ang had always disliked Chao Cuo. Whenever Chao Cuo was present, Ang would leave.
units.literal: Ang had always disliked Chao Cuo. Whenever Chao Cuo was present and seated, Ang would leave.

units.zh: 盎坐，錯亦去：兩人未嘗同堂語。
units.en: When Ang was present, Cuo would likewise depart. The two never spoke in the same room.
units.literal: When Ang was seated, Cuo would likewise leave. The two never exchanged a word in the same hall.

units.zh: 及孝文帝崩，孝景帝即位，鼂錯為御史大夫，使吏案袁盎受吳王財物，抵罪，詔赦以為庶人。
units.en: When Emperor Wen died and Emperor Jing came to the throne, Chao Cuo was appointed Imperial Secretary. He sent officials to investigate Yuan Ang for accepting gifts from the King of Wu, and Ang was convicted. By imperial edict he was pardoned but reduced to a commoner.
units.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen died and Emperor Xiaojing ascended the throne, Chao Cuo became the Imperial Secretary. He dispatched officials to investigate Yuan Ang for accepting gifts from the King of Wu, and Ang was convicted. By imperial edict he was pardoned but reduced to the status of a commoner.

units.zh: 吳楚反，聞，鼂錯謂丞史曰：「夫袁盎多受吳王金錢，專為蔽匿，言不反。
units.en: When Wu and Chu rebelled, upon hearing the news, Chao Cuo said to the Chancellor's Clerk, 'Yuan Ang accepted large sums from the King of Wu and deliberately covered for him, insisting he would not rebel.
units.literal: When Wu and Chu rebelled, upon hearing the news, Chao Cuo said to the Chancellor's Clerk: 'Yuan Ang accepted large sums of gold and money from the King of Wu and deliberately concealed and covered for him, claiming he would not rebel.

units.zh: 今果反，欲請治盎宜知計謀。」
units.en: Now that the rebellion has come, I intend to request an investigation of Ang, who surely knew of the plot.'
units.literal: Now he has indeed rebelled. I wish to request an investigation of Ang, who must have known of the plot.'

units.zh: 丞史曰：「事未發，治之有絕。
units.en: The Chancellor's Clerk replied, 'Before the rebellion broke out, an investigation might have nipped it in the bud.
units.literal: The Chancellor's Clerk said: 'Before the affair broke out, pursuing it might have put an end to it.

units.zh: 今兵西鄉，治之何益！
units.en: Now that their armies are marching west, what good would an investigation do!
units.literal: Now that the armies are marching westward, what good would an investigation do!

units.zh: 且袁盎不宜有謀。」
units.en: Besides, it is unlikely that Yuan Ang was party to the conspiracy.'
units.literal: Moreover, Yuan Ang is unlikely to have been party to the plot.'

units.zh: 鼂錯猶與未決。
units.en: Chao Cuo hesitated and could not make up his mind.
units.literal: Chao Cuo still hesitated and had not yet decided.

units.zh: 人有告袁盎者，袁盎恐，夜見竇嬰，為言吳所以反者，願至上前口對狀。
units.en: Someone warned Yuan Ang. Alarmed, Ang went to see Dou Ying that night. He explained the reasons for Wu's rebellion and expressed his wish to present his case in person before the Emperor.
units.literal: Someone informed Yuan Ang of this. Ang was alarmed and went to see Dou Ying by night. He explained the reasons for Wu's rebellion and expressed his wish to present an oral defense before the Emperor.

units.zh: 竇嬰入言上，上乃召袁盎入見。
units.en: Dou Ying went in and spoke to the Emperor, who summoned Yuan Ang for an audience.
units.literal: Dou Ying went in and spoke to the Emperor, and the Emperor thereupon summoned Yuan Ang for an audience.

units.zh: 鼂錯在前，及盎請辟人賜閒，錯去，固恨甚。
units.en: Chao Cuo was present at the audience. When Ang asked that others be dismissed for a private word, Cuo had to leave, and his resentment deepened.
units.literal: Chao Cuo was present at the time. When Ang requested that others be dismissed for a private audience, Cuo was forced to withdraw, and his resentment deepened greatly.

units.zh: 袁盎具言吳所以反狀，以錯故，獨急斬錯以謝吳，吳兵乃可罷。
units.en: Yuan Ang laid out in full the reasons for Wu's rebellion, arguing that Cuo was the cause, and that the only way to halt the Wu armies was to execute Cuo at once as a gesture of appeasement to Wu.
units.literal: Yuan Ang laid out in full the reasons for Wu's rebellion, arguing that it was on account of Cuo, and that the only course was to swiftly execute Cuo as an apology to Wu, after which the Wu armies could be halted.

units.zh: 其語具在吳事中。
units.en: The full account of his words can be found in the chapter on the affairs of Wu.
units.literal: The full account of his words is in the chapter on the affairs of Wu.

units.zh: 使袁盎為太常，竇嬰為大將軍。
units.en: The emperor made Yuan Ang Grand Master of Ceremonies and Dou Ying Grand General.
units.literal: Yuan Ang was appointed Grand Master of Ceremonies, and Dou Ying was made Grand General.

units.zh: 兩人素相與善。
units.en: The two had always been close.
units.literal: The two had always been on good terms with each other.

units.zh: 逮吳反。
units.en: Then Wu rose in rebellion.
units.literal: This was at the time of the Wu rebellion.

units.zh: 諸陵長者長安中賢大夫爭附兩人，車隨者日數百乘。
units.en: The elders of the mausoleum towns and the eminent officials of Chang'an vied to attach themselves to the two men, and hundreds of carriages trailed them each day.
units.literal: The elders of the various imperial mausoleum towns and the worthy officials of Chang'an all vied to attach themselves to the two men. Hundreds of carriages followed them each day.

units.zh: 及鼂錯已誅，袁盎以太常使吳。
units.en: After Chao Cuo was executed, Yuan Ang was dispatched as Grand Master of Ceremonies on a mission to Wu.
units.literal: After Chao Cuo had been executed, Yuan Ang was sent as Grand Master of Ceremonies on a mission to Wu.

units.zh: 吳王欲使將，不肯。
units.en: The King of Wu wanted to make him a general, but Ang refused.
units.literal: The King of Wu wished to make him a general, but he refused.

units.zh: 欲殺之，使一都尉以五百人圍守盎軍中。
units.en: The king wanted to kill him and sent a commandant with five hundred soldiers to surround and guard Ang in the camp.
units.literal: The king wished to kill him, and dispatched a commandant with five hundred men to surround and guard Ang in the military camp.

units.zh: 袁盎自其為吳相時，（嘗）有從史嘗盜愛盎侍兒，盎知之，弗泄，遇之如故。
units.en: When Yuan Ang had served as Chancellor of Wu, one of his attendant clerks had secretly carried on with a maidservant Ang favored. Ang knew of it but said nothing, treating the man just as before.
units.literal: When Yuan Ang had served as Chancellor of Wu, one of his attendant clerks had secretly taken a maidservant whom Ang favored. Ang knew of it but did not expose the matter, treating the clerk just as before.

units.zh: 人有告從史，言「君知爾與侍者通」，乃亡歸。
units.en: Someone told the clerk, 'Your lord knows you have been carrying on with his maid.' The clerk fled and went home.
units.literal: Someone told the attendant clerk: 'Your lord knows that you have been carrying on with his maid.' The clerk thereupon fled and returned home.

units.zh: 袁盎驅自追之，遂以侍者賜之，復為從史。
units.en: Yuan Ang rode after him, gave him the maidservant, and reinstated him as an attendant clerk.
units.literal: Yuan Ang raced after him on horseback and gave him the maidservant, and the clerk resumed his post as attendant.

units.zh: 及袁盎使吳見守，從史適為守盎校尉司馬，乃悉以其裝齎置二石醇醪，會天寒，士卒饑渴，飲酒醉，西南陬卒皆臥，司馬夜引袁盎起，曰：「君可以去矣，吳王期旦日斬君。」
units.en: When Yuan Ang was sent to Wu and placed under guard, the former clerk happened to be serving as the Colonel and Commander in charge of guarding him. He used all his belongings to buy two dan of strong wine. As it was bitterly cold, the soldiers were hungry and thirsty. They drank the wine and fell into a stupor; the soldiers at the southwest corner all passed out. In the dead of night, the Commander roused Yuan Ang and said, 'You must leave at once. The King of Wu plans to behead you at dawn.'
units.literal: When Yuan Ang was sent to Wu and placed under guard, the attendant clerk happened to be serving as the Colonel and Commander in charge of guarding Ang. He used all his supplies to procure two dan of strong wine. As it happened, the weather was bitterly cold, and the soldiers were hungry and thirsty. They drank the wine and became drunk, and the soldiers at the southwest corner all fell asleep. The Commander roused Yuan Ang in the night and said: 'You must leave now. The King of Wu plans to behead you at dawn.'

units.zh: 盎弗信，曰：「公何為者？」
units.en: Ang did not believe him and said, 'Sir, what are you about?'
units.literal: Ang did not believe him and said, 'Sir, what is this about?'

units.zh: 司馬曰：「臣故為從史盜君侍兒者。」
units.en: The Commander replied, 'I am the former attendant clerk who carried on with your maidservant.'
units.literal: The Commander said: 'I am the former attendant clerk who stole your maidservant.'

units.zh: 盎乃驚謝曰；
units.en: Ang was stunned and said gratefully:
units.literal: Ang was startled and expressed his gratitude, saying:

units.zh: 「公幸有親，吾不足以累公。」
units.en: 'You have a family. I could not bear to bring trouble upon you on my account.'
units.literal: 'You fortunately have a family. I could not bear to bring trouble upon you.'

units.zh: 司馬曰：「君弟去，臣亦且亡，辟吾親，君何患！」
units.en: The Commander said, 'Just go, my lord. I will flee as well and hide my family. You need not worry about me!'
units.literal: The Commander said: 'Just go, my lord. I too will flee and take my family into hiding. What have you to worry about!'

units.zh: 乃以刀決張，道從醉卒（直）隧［直］出。
units.en: He slashed open the tent with his sword and led Ang through the passage past the drunken soldiers and out into the open.
units.literal: He then cut open the tent with his sword and led Ang through the passage past the drunken soldiers and straight out.

units.zh: 司馬與分背，袁盎解節毛懷之，杖，步行七八里，明，見梁騎，騎馳去，遂歸報。
units.en: The Commander and Ang parted ways. Ang stripped the tassels from his tally, hid it inside his robe, took up a walking stick, and walked seven or eight li on foot. At dawn, he spotted cavalry from Liang. He galloped off with them and returned to deliver his report.
units.literal: The Commander and Ang parted ways. Ang removed the tassels from his tally, tucked the tally in his robe, took up a walking stick, and walked seven or eight li on foot. At dawn, he spotted Liang cavalry. He rode off at a gallop and returned to make his report.

units.zh: 吳楚已破，上更以元王子平陸侯禮為楚王，袁盎為楚相。
units.en: After Wu and Chu were defeated, the Emperor installed the Marquis of Pinglu, Li, a son of the former King Yuan, as the new King of Chu, and Yuan Ang was appointed Chancellor of Chu.
units.literal: After Wu and Chu had been defeated, the Emperor installed the Marquis of Pinglu, Li, son of the former King Yuan, as the new King of Chu, and Yuan Ang was made Chancellor of Chu.

units.zh: 嘗上書有所言，不用。
units.en: He once submitted a memorial with proposals, but they were not adopted.
units.literal: He once submitted a memorial speaking on certain matters, but his proposals were not adopted.

units.zh: 袁盎病免居家，與閭里浮沈，相隨行，鬬雞走狗。
units.en: Yuan Ang was dismissed on grounds of illness and retired to his home. He drifted along with his neighbors, joining them in cockfights and dog races.
units.literal: Yuan Ang was dismissed due to illness and lived at home. He drifted along with his neighbors, going about with them, cockfighting and dog-racing.

units.zh: 雒陽劇孟嘗過袁盎，盎善待之。
units.en: Ju Meng of Luoyang once paid Yuan Ang a visit, and Ang received him warmly.
units.literal: Ju Meng of Luoyang once visited Yuan Ang, and Ang treated him well.

units.zh: 安陵富人有謂盎曰：「吾聞劇孟博徒，將軍何自通之？」
units.en: A wealthy man of Anling said to Ang, 'I hear that Ju Meng is a gambler. Why do you associate with such a man, General?'
units.literal: A wealthy man of Anling said to Ang: 'I have heard that Ju Meng is a gambler. Why does the General associate with such a man?'

units.zh: 盎曰：「劇孟雖博徒，然母死，客送葬車千餘乘，此亦有過人者。
units.en: Ang replied, 'Though Ju Meng is a gambler, when his mother died, over a thousand carriages of guests attended the funeral. A man who commands such loyalty has qualities that surpass the ordinary.
units.literal: Ang said: 'Though Ju Meng is a gambler, when his mother died, more than a thousand carriages of guests attended the funeral procession. This shows he has qualities that surpass those of ordinary men.

units.zh: 且緩急人所有。
units.en: After all, crises come to every man.
units.literal: Moreover, emergencies are something that everyone faces.

units.zh: 夫一旦有急叩門，不以親為解，不以存亡為辭，天下所望者，獨季心、劇孟耳。
units.en: When a crisis comes knocking, men who will not hide behind family ties or plead for their own lives—men whom all under heaven look to—are only Ji Xin and Ju Meng.
units.literal: When one day a crisis comes knocking at the door, those who will not use family ties as an excuse and will not plead concerns of life and death—the men whom all under heaven look to—are only Ji Xin and Ju Meng.

units.zh: 今公常從數騎，一旦有緩急，寧足恃乎！」
units.en: You ride with only a few horsemen. If a crisis comes, can you rely on them!'
units.literal: Now you go about with only a few horsemen. If one day a crisis comes, can they be relied upon!'

units.zh: 罵富人，弗與通。
units.en: He berated the rich man and cut off all contact with him.
units.literal: He berated the wealthy man and refused to associate with him.

units.zh: 諸公聞之，皆多袁盎。
units.en: When word of this spread, everyone praised Yuan Ang.
units.literal: When the various gentlemen heard of this, they all praised Yuan Ang.

units.zh: 袁盎雖家居，景帝時時使人問籌策。
units.en: Although Yuan Ang was living in retirement, Emperor Jing would from time to time send someone to consult him on matters of policy.
units.literal: Although Yuan Ang was living at home, Emperor Jing would from time to time send people to consult him for counsel and strategies.

units.zh: 梁王欲求為嗣，袁盎進說，其後語塞。
units.en: When the King of Liang sought to be named heir, Yuan Ang spoke against it, and the matter was dropped.
units.literal: When the King of Liang sought to be named heir, Yuan Ang spoke out against it, and thereafter the discussion was silenced.

units.zh: 梁王以此怨盎，曾使人刺盎。
units.en: The King of Liang bore a grudge against Ang and sent assassins after him.
units.literal: The King of Liang bore a grudge against Ang for this and sent someone to assassinate him.

units.zh: 刺者至關中，問袁盎，諸君譽之皆不容口。
units.en: When the assassin arrived in Guanzhong and asked about Yuan Ang, everyone he met praised Ang so effusively they could scarcely contain themselves.
units.literal: When the assassin arrived at Guanzhong and inquired about Yuan Ang, everyone praised him so effusively that they could hardly contain themselves.

units.zh: 乃見袁盎曰：「臣受梁王金來刺君，君長者，不忍刺君。
units.en: He went to see Yuan Ang and said, 'I was paid by the King of Liang to assassinate you. But you are an honorable man, and I cannot bring myself to do it.
units.literal: He then went to see Yuan Ang and said: 'I accepted gold from the King of Liang and came to assassinate you. But you are an honorable man, and I cannot bring myself to do it.

units.zh: 然後刺君者十餘曹，備之！」
units.en: But there are more than ten other teams of assassins coming for you. Be on your guard!'
units.literal: However, more than ten other teams of assassins are coming after you. Be on your guard!'

units.zh: 袁盎心不樂，家又多怪，乃之棓生所問占。
units.en: Yuan Ang was deeply troubled, and strange omens had been plaguing his household. He went to consult the diviner Master Pou.
units.literal: Yuan Ang was troubled at heart, and his household had been plagued by many strange occurrences. He went to consult the diviner Master Pou.

units.zh: 還，梁刺客後曹輩果遮刺殺盎安陵郭門外。
units.en: On his way back, the later teams of Liang assassins ambushed and killed Ang outside the outer gate of Anling.
units.literal: On his way back, the later teams of Liang assassins indeed ambushed and stabbed Ang to death outside the outer gate of Anling.

units.zh: 鼂錯者，潁川人也。
units.en: Chao Cuo was a native of Yingchuan.
units.literal: Chao Cuo was a native of Yingchuan.

units.zh: 學申商刑名於軹張恢先所，與雒陽宋孟及劉禮同師。
units.en: He studied the Legalist doctrines of Shen Buhai and Shang Yang under the elder Zhang Hui of Zhi, together with Song Meng of Luoyang and Liu Li.
units.literal: He studied the Legalist teachings of Shen Buhai and Shang Yang under the tutelage of the elder Zhang Hui of Zhi, together with Song Meng of Luoyang and Liu Li as fellow students.

units.zh: 以文學為太常掌故。
units.en: On account of his scholarship, he was appointed Keeper of Records under the Grand Master of Ceremonies.
units.literal: On account of his learning, he was appointed as a Keeper of Records under the Grand Master of Ceremonies.

units.zh: 錯為人陗直刻深。
units.en: Cuo was by nature severe, blunt, and unsparing.
units.literal: Cuo was by nature harsh, blunt, exacting, and unforgiving.

units.zh: 孝文帝時，天下無治尚書者，獨聞濟南伏生故秦博士，治尚書，年九十餘，老不可徵，乃詔太常使人往受之。
units.en: In the time of Emperor Wen, no one in the realm still studied the Book of Documents. The only master known to survive was Fu Sheng of Jinan, a former Erudite of the Qin, who was over ninety and too old to be summoned to court. An edict was issued ordering the Grand Master of Ceremonies to send someone to study under him.
units.literal: In the time of Emperor Xiaowen, there was no one in the realm who studied the Book of Documents. It was heard only that Fu Sheng of Jinan, a former Erudite of the Qin, had mastered it. He was over ninety years old and too aged to be summoned to court, so an edict was issued ordering the Grand Master of Ceremonies to send someone to receive his teachings.

units.zh: 太常遣錯受尚書伏生所。
units.en: The Grand Master of Ceremonies dispatched Cuo to study the Book of Documents under Fu Sheng.
units.literal: The Grand Master of Ceremonies sent Cuo to study the Book of Documents under Fu Sheng.

units.zh: 還，因上便宜事，以書稱說。
units.en: Upon his return, he submitted proposals on matters of governance, citing the Book of Documents to support his arguments.
units.literal: Upon his return, he submitted proposals on expedient measures, citing the Book of Documents to support his arguments.

units.zh: 詔以為太子舍人、門大夫、家令。
units.en: By imperial edict, he was successively appointed Retainer of the Heir Apparent, Gentleman of the Gate, and Steward of the Household.
units.literal: By imperial edict, he was appointed successively as Retainer of the Heir Apparent, Gentleman of the Gate, and Steward of the Household.

units.zh: 以其辯得幸太子，太子家號曰「智囊」。
units.en: Through his eloquence he won the favor of the Heir Apparent, and the household dubbed him the 'Bag of Wisdom.'
units.literal: Through his eloquence he won the favor of the Heir Apparent, and in the Heir Apparent's household he was called the 'Bag of Wisdom.'

units.zh: 數上書孝文時，言削諸侯事，及法令可更定者。
units.en: He submitted numerous memorials during Emperor Wen's reign, arguing for the reduction of the feudal lords' territories and proposing revisions to the laws.
units.literal: He submitted numerous memorials during Emperor Xiaowen's reign, arguing for the reduction of the feudal lords' territories and proposing revisions to the laws and regulations.

units.zh: 書數十上，孝文不聽，然奇其材，遷為中大夫。
units.en: He submitted dozens of memorials, but Emperor Wen did not adopt his proposals. The Emperor admired his talent, however, and promoted him to Palace Grandee.
units.literal: He submitted dozens of memorials, but Emperor Xiaowen did not adopt his proposals. Nevertheless, the Emperor admired his talents and promoted him to the rank of Palace Grandee.

units.zh: 當是時，太子善錯計策，袁盎諸大功臣多不好錯。
units.en: At that time, the Heir Apparent approved of Cuo's plans and strategies, but Yuan Ang and many of the senior meritorious ministers disliked him.
units.literal: At that time, the Heir Apparent approved of Cuo's plans and strategies, but Yuan Ang and many of the great meritorious ministers disliked Cuo.

units.zh: 景帝即位，以錯為內史。
units.en: When Emperor Jing came to the throne, he appointed Cuo as Prefect of the Capital.
units.literal: When Emperor Jing ascended the throne, he appointed Cuo as Prefect of the Capital.

units.zh: 錯常數請閒言事，輒聽，寵幸傾九卿，法令多所更定。
units.en: Cuo frequently requested private audiences to discuss affairs, and the Emperor always listened. His favor eclipsed that of the Nine Ministers, and many laws and regulations were revised at his behest.
units.literal: Cuo frequently requested private audiences to discuss affairs, and the Emperor invariably heeded him. His favor eclipsed that of the Nine Ministers, and many laws and regulations were revised.

units.zh: 丞相申屠嘉心弗便，力未有以傷。
units.en: Chancellor Shentu Jia resented this but lacked the means to bring Cuo down.
units.literal: Chancellor Shentu Jia was displeased in his heart but did not yet have the power to harm Cuo.

units.zh: 內史府居太上廟壖中，門東出，不便，錯乃穿兩門南出，鑿廟壖垣。
units.en: The offices of the Prefect of the Capital stood within the precincts of the Supreme Temple. The gate faced east, which was inconvenient, so Cuo opened two gates facing south, cutting through the temple precinct wall.
units.literal: The offices of the Prefect of the Capital were located within the precincts of the Supreme Temple. The gate opened to the east, which was inconvenient. Cuo therefore opened two gates to the south, cutting through the precinct wall of the temple.

units.zh: 丞相嘉聞，大怒，欲因此過為奏請誅錯。
units.en: When Chancellor Jia heard of this, he was furious and resolved to use the offense as grounds for a memorial requesting Cuo's execution.
units.literal: When Chancellor Jia heard of this, he was furious and intended to use this transgression as the basis for a memorial requesting Cuo's execution.

units.zh: 錯聞之，即夜請閒，具為上言之。
units.en: When Cuo learned of the Chancellor's plan, he immediately sought a private audience that night and laid the whole matter before the Emperor.
units.literal: When Cuo heard of this, he immediately requested a private audience that very night and laid the entire matter before the Emperor.

units.zh: 丞相奏事，因言錯擅鑿廟垣為門，請下廷尉誅。
units.en: When the Chancellor presented his memorial, he charged Cuo with arbitrarily cutting through the temple wall to make a gate and requested that the case be referred to the Commandant of Justice for execution.
units.literal: When the Chancellor presented his memorial, he accused Cuo of arbitrarily cutting through the temple wall to make a gate and requested that the case be referred to the Commandant of Justice for execution.

units.zh: 上曰：「此非廟垣，乃壖中垣，不致於法。」
units.en: The Emperor replied, 'That is not the temple wall itself but merely the precinct wall. No law applies.'
units.literal: The Emperor said: 'This is not the temple wall itself, but rather the precinct wall. The law does not apply.'

units.zh: 丞相謝。
units.en: The Chancellor apologized.
units.literal: The Chancellor apologized.

units.zh: 罷朝，怒謂長史曰：「吾當先斬以聞，乃先請，為兒所賣，固誤。」
units.en: After court was dismissed, he angrily said to the Chief Clerk, 'I should have had him beheaded first and reported afterward. Instead, I asked permission first and was outmaneuvered by that boy. A terrible blunder.'
units.literal: After court was dismissed, he angrily said to the Chief Clerk: 'I should have had him beheaded first and reported afterward. Instead I asked permission first and was outmaneuvered by that boy. It was a great blunder.'

units.zh: 丞相遂發病死。
units.en: The Chancellor soon fell ill and died.
units.literal: The Chancellor thereupon fell ill and died.

units.zh: 錯以此愈貴。
units.en: After this, Cuo's power only grew.
units.literal: Cuo became even more influential because of this.

units.zh: 遷為御史大夫，請諸侯之罪過，削其地，收其枝郡。
units.en: He was promoted to Imperial Secretary. He proposed charging the feudal lords with their offenses, reducing their territories, and confiscating their outlying commanderies.
units.literal: He was promoted to Imperial Secretary. He requested that the feudal lords be charged with their offenses, their territories reduced, and their outlying commanderies confiscated.

units.zh: 奏上，上令公卿列侯宗室集議，莫敢難，獨竇嬰爭之，由此與錯有卻。
units.en: When the memorial was submitted, the Emperor ordered the senior officials, marquises, and members of the imperial clan to deliberate. None dared object, except Dou Ying, who contested it. From this a rift grew between him and Cuo.
units.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the Emperor ordered the senior officials, marquises, and members of the imperial clan to deliberate on it. None dared to object, except Dou Ying, who contested it. From this a rift developed between Dou Ying and Cuo.

units.zh: 錯所更令三十章，諸侯皆諠譁疾鼂錯。
units.en: Cuo revised thirty articles of law. The feudal lords all raised an outcry and despised Chao Cuo.
units.literal: Cuo's revised laws amounted to thirty articles. The feudal lords all protested loudly and despised Chao Cuo.

units.zh: 錯父聞之，從潁川來，謂錯曰：「上初即位，公為政用事，侵削諸侯，別疏人骨肉，人口議多怨公者，何也？」
units.en: When Cuo's father heard of this, he came from Yingchuan and said to Cuo, 'The Emperor has only just come to the throne, and you are the one directing affairs of state. You encroach upon the feudal lords, reduce their lands, and drive a wedge between the Emperor's own kin. People everywhere are speaking against you with resentment. Why?'
units.literal: When Cuo's father heard of this, he came from Yingchuan and said to Cuo: 'The Emperor has only just come to the throne, and you are the one directing affairs of state. You encroach upon and reduce the feudal lords, separating and estranging the Emperor's own flesh and blood. People's talk is full of resentment toward you. Why is this?'

units.zh: 鼂錯曰：「固也。
units.en: Chao Cuo replied, 'That is to be expected.
units.literal: Chao Cuo said: 'That is to be expected.

units.zh: 不如此，天子不尊，宗廟不安。」
units.en: Without this, the Son of Heaven cannot be honored, and the ancestral temples will never be secure.'
units.literal: Without this, the Son of Heaven cannot be honored, and the ancestral temples cannot be secure.'

units.zh: 錯父曰：「劉氏安矣，而鼂氏危矣，吾去公歸矣！」
units.en: Cuo's father said, 'The House of Liu may be secure, but the House of Chao is in peril. I will leave you and go home!'
units.literal: Cuo's father said: 'The House of Liu is secure, but the House of Chao is in peril. I shall leave you and go home!'

units.zh: 遂飲藥死，曰：「吾不忍見禍及吾身。」
units.en: He then drank poison and died, saying, 'I cannot bear to live to see disaster fall upon me.'
units.literal: He then drank poison and died, saying: 'I cannot bear to see disaster reach my own person.'

units.zh: 死十餘日，吳楚七國果反，以誅錯為名。
units.en: A little over ten days after his death, the seven kingdoms of Wu and Chu rose in rebellion, using the demand to execute Cuo as their pretext.
units.literal: More than ten days after his death, the seven kingdoms of Wu and Chu did indeed rebel, using the demand to execute Cuo as their pretext.

units.zh: 及竇嬰、袁盎進說，上令鼂錯衣朝衣斬東市。
units.en: When Dou Ying and Yuan Ang pressed their case, the Emperor ordered Chao Cuo beheaded in his court robes at the Eastern Market.
units.literal: When Dou Ying and Yuan Ang came forward with their arguments, the Emperor ordered Chao Cuo to be beheaded in his court robes at the Eastern Market.

units.zh: 鼂錯已死，謁者仆射鄧公為校尉，擊吳楚軍為將。
units.en: After Chao Cuo was dead, Deng Gong, the Chief Receptionist, served as a Colonel and led troops against the Wu and Chu armies.
units.literal: After Chao Cuo was dead, Deng Gong, the Chief Receptionist, was serving as a Colonel and led troops as a general to attack the Wu and Chu armies.

units.zh: 還，上書言軍事，謁見上。
units.en: Upon his return, he submitted a memorial on military affairs and was granted an audience with the Emperor.
units.literal: Upon his return, he submitted a memorial on military affairs and requested an audience with the Emperor.

units.zh: 上問曰：「道軍所來，聞鼂錯死，吳楚罷不？」
units.en: The Emperor asked, 'On your way back from the front, did you hear whether Wu and Chu ceased hostilities after Chao Cuo's death?'
units.literal: The Emperor asked: 'On your way back from the army, did you hear whether, after Chao Cuo's death, Wu and Chu have ceased hostilities?'

units.zh: 鄧公曰：「吳王為反數十年矣，發怒削地，以誅錯為名，其意非在錯也。
units.en: Deng Gong replied, 'The King of Wu has been plotting rebellion for decades. He exploded in fury over the reduction of his territory and used the execution of Cuo as his pretext. His true aim was never about Cuo.
units.literal: Deng Gong said: 'The King of Wu has been plotting rebellion for decades. He erupted in fury over the reduction of his territory and used the demand to execute Cuo as his pretext. His true intention was never about Cuo.

units.zh: 且臣恐天下之士噤口，不敢復言也！」
units.en: Moreover, I fear that the scholars of the realm will seal their lips and never dare speak again!'
units.literal: Moreover, I fear that the scholars of the realm will clamp their mouths shut and never dare to speak again!'

units.zh: 上曰：「何哉？」
units.en: The Emperor asked, 'Why?'
units.literal: The Emperor said: 'Why is that?'

units.zh: 鄧公曰：「夫鼂錯患諸侯彊大不可制，故請削地以尊京師，萬世之利也。
units.en: Deng Gong said, 'Chao Cuo saw that the feudal lords had grown too powerful to control, and so he proposed reducing their territories to strengthen the capital. This was a policy to benefit ten thousand generations.
units.literal: Deng Gong said: 'Chao Cuo was concerned that the feudal lords had grown too strong to be controlled, and so he proposed reducing their territories to enhance the authority of the capital. This was a policy that would benefit ten thousand generations.

units.zh: 計畫始行，卒受大戮，內杜忠臣之口，外為諸侯報仇，臣竊為陛下不取也。」
units.en: His plans had barely begun when he met a terrible end. At home, this has sealed the mouths of loyal ministers. Abroad, it has served as the feudal lords' revenge. I venture to say that this was not a wise course for Your Majesty.'
units.literal: His plans had only just begun to be carried out when he met with terrible execution. Internally, this has sealed the mouths of loyal ministers. Externally, it has served as revenge for the feudal lords. I venture to say that this was inadvisable for Your Majesty.'

units.zh: 於是景帝默然良久，曰：「公言善，吾亦恨之。」
units.en: Emperor Jing fell silent for a long while, then said, 'You speak well. I, too, regret it.'
units.literal: At this, Emperor Jing was silent for a long time and then said: 'Your words are well spoken. I too regret it.'

units.zh: 乃拜鄧公為城陽中尉。
units.en: Deng Gong was then appointed Commandant of Chengyang.
units.literal: He then appointed Deng Gong as Commandant of Chengyang.

units.zh: 鄧公，成固人也，多奇計。
units.en: Deng Gong was a native of Chenggu, known for his many brilliant stratagems.
units.literal: Deng Gong was a native of Chenggu and was known for his many remarkable stratagems.

units.zh: 建元中，上招賢良，公卿言鄧公，時鄧公免，起家為九卿。
units.en: During the Jianyuan period, when the Emperor sought worthy men, the senior officials recommended Deng Gong. At the time he was out of office, but he was recalled and appointed as one of the Nine Ministers.
units.literal: During the Jianyuan period, when the Emperor sought worthy and talented men, the senior officials recommended Deng Gong. At that time Deng Gong was out of office. He was recalled from private life and appointed as one of the Nine Ministers.

units.zh: 一年，復謝病免歸。
units.en: After a year, he again pleaded illness and retired.
units.literal: After one year, he again pleaded illness and was dismissed, returning home.

units.zh: 其子章以修黃老言顯於諸公閒。
units.en: His son Zhang became prominent among the senior officials through his devotion to the teachings of Huang-Lao.
units.literal: His son Zhang became prominent among the senior officials through his study and practice of the teachings of the Yellow Emperor and Laozi.

units.zh: 太史公曰：袁盎雖不好學，亦善傅會，仁心為質，引義慨。
units.en: The Grand Historian remarks: Though Yuan Ang was no scholar, he was adept at applying ideas to the moment. His character was grounded in benevolence, and he invoked righteousness with passionate conviction.
units.literal: The Grand Historian remarks: Although Yuan Ang was not fond of learning, he was skilled at connecting ideas and applying them to the moment. His character was rooted in benevolence, and he drew upon righteousness to speak with passion.

units.zh: 遭孝文初立，資適逢世。
units.en: He had the fortune to serve at the beginning of Emperor Wen's reign, and his qualities were well suited to the times.
units.literal: He happened to encounter the early accession of Emperor Xiaowen, and his talents were well suited to the times.

units.zh: 時以變易，及吳楚一說，說雖行哉，然復不遂。
units.en: But the times shifted. When the Wu-Chu crisis came, his counsel was adopted, yet it did not ultimately achieve its purpose.
units.literal: But the times shifted and changed. When the Wu-Chu crisis came, his counsel, though adopted, did not ultimately achieve its end.

units.zh: 好聲矜賢，竟以名敗。
units.en: He loved reputation and prided himself on his virtue, and in the end it was his very fame that brought about his ruin.
units.literal: He loved reputation and prided himself on his virtue, and in the end it was his fame that brought about his downfall.

units.zh: 鼂錯為家令時，數言事不用；
units.en: When Chao Cuo served as Steward of the Household, he repeatedly offered proposals that went unheeded.
units.literal: When Chao Cuo served as Steward of the Household, he repeatedly spoke on affairs of state, but his proposals were not adopted.

units.zh: 後擅權，多所變更。
units.en: Later he seized power and made sweeping changes.
units.literal: Later he monopolized power and changed many things.

units.zh: 諸侯發難，不急匡救，欲報私讎，反以亡軀。
units.en: When the feudal lords rose in revolt, rather than urgently seeking to set things right, he tried to settle a private grudge—and lost his life for it.
units.literal: When the feudal lords raised their revolt, he did not urgently seek to rescue the situation but wished to settle a private grudge, and instead lost his own life.

units.zh: 語曰「變古亂常，不死則亡」，豈錯等謂邪！
units.en: As the saying goes, 'Those who overturn the old ways and disrupt the established order will either die or be ruined.' Was this not said of men like Cuo!
units.literal: The saying goes, 'Those who alter the old ways and disrupt the established order, if they do not die, will be ruined.' Was this not spoken of men like Cuo!
